text:
这是把同一套 Helm One 路演内容重排进官方答辩模板后的 15 页 PPT（26.67×15 英寸，1920×1080 渲染）。模板规范：白底；右上橙色 MI logo；内容页左上青色小眉题「PROJECT DEFENSE · 项目答辩」；40pt 近黑标题 + 青→紫渐变短线；浅灰圆角卡；底部细分隔线 + 右下「2026 首届 openvela AI 硬件开发者大赛」；封面/致谢为黑底光带。

请完整逐页验收（用户标准：能直接上台讲，且像官方模板做出来的）。重点：
1) 文字是否溢出/被裁切/压卡边，中文断行是否别扭；
2) 卡片是否等高、对齐、留白均匀；渐变短线/MI logo/页脚位置是否全篇一致；
3) 截图/地图/GIF 首帧是否变形、被裁、比例正确；
4) 封面与致谢的黑底图上文字对比度、位置是否稳；
5) 有没有「模板元素被压扁/拉伸」的痕迹。

PNG：/home/jinsc/SDK/vela/ppt/.build/render_tpl/s-01.png 至 s-15.png。

每页一行 JSON：{"page":N,"verdict":"pass|fail","issues":["具体到元素与位置"],"fix":"一句可执行修法"}。最后一句总体判断。

thinking:
Let me start by reading the assigned page images one by one. There are 15 pages: /home/jinsc/SDK/vela/ppt/.build/render_tpl/s-01.png through s-15.png.

I'll read them and give verdicts per the user's requested JSON format: {"page":N,"verdict":"pass|fail","issues":[...],"fix":"..."} plus a final overall judgment sentence.

Let me read the images. I can batch independent reads in one block. But the instructions say "Read your page images one by one, writing each page's verdict immediately after reading it." However, batching reads is fine for efficiency; but the workflow says one by one with verdict written immediately after reading. I'll read a few at a time and note verdicts as I go. To be safe and thorough, I'll read them in small batches (they're independent), then produce the final output in page order at the end. Actually the system prompt says write each page's verdict immediately after reading it — I can do that in the text between tool calls.

Let me start reading.

Page 1: Cover — black background with light band (infinity ribbon + sailboat). MI logo top right orange, present. Title "Helm One" white large, subtitle line, small tagline. Text contrast good. The eyebrow "2026 首届 openvela AI 硬件开发者大赛" with gradient short line — consistent. Position looks stable. No overflow. Pass.

Page 2: Content page. Eyebrow "PROJECT DEFENSE · 项目答辩" top-left cyan, title "车把上，不需要一块手机" 40pt near-black, gradient short line below. Three cards equal height. But cards are quite empty at bottom — cards 02 and 03 have one line of text while card 01 has two lines; bottom half of cards is empty. Is that "a single card or container left half empty"? All three cards are uniformly half empty actually — the cards are tall with text only in the top ~40%. The cards are equal height and aligned. The empty bottom space is consistent across all three, so it reads as intentional whitespace, though quite generous. Hmm. The pptx guidance says "a single card or container left half empty (that too is uneven visual distribution)". Here all three are equally empty at bottom — uniform, so it's a design choice of whitespace. But is it "crammed" or imbalanced? The cards occupy a big area, text top-aligned. It looks acceptable, though somewhat empty. There's also a bottom conclusion line "抬头 0.5 秒，看清一个数。" with subtext. Footer line + right bottom text present. MI logo top right present.

Verdict: pass, though I might note the large empty bottom half of cards. The user asks about card equal height, alignment, uniform whitespace — they are equal. I'll pass it. Actually, let me consider: "one side overloaded while the other sits empty" — no. "a single card or container left half empty" — all three are half empty uniformly; consistent. It's a stylistic minimal look. I'd call it pass but could mention. The user's criterion is acceptance: ready to present. I'll pass.

Continue reading pages 3-4.

Page 3: Four cards, equal height/width, aligned. Big stat numbers, subtitle, one-line body. Bottom half of cards empty but uniform. Cards take upper ~55% of the content area; lower area is empty white — noticeable bottom whitespace but not broken. Text fits. Pass. Actually there's a fairly large empty area below cards (from y~680 to footer ~845). It's whitespace, not imbalance per se. Consistent with page 2 style? Page 2 had cards to ~680 too plus bottom text. Page 3 lacks bottom text, so slightly emptier. Acceptable.

Page 4: Three cards with labels 感知/计算/显现, plus 4 stat columns below. Cards equal height. Bottom line of small text. Looks fine. Card text top area with ~half empty below, uniform. The stat row: "240 MHz / 512 KB / 16 MB / 240×320" aligned. Fine. Pass.

Continue 5-6.

Page 5: Stacked list rows (APP/LINK/HELM/BSP/OS/SoC). Rows aligned, uniform. OS row is dark highlight — intentional emphasis. Right side stats 20 / 6 / 6 类. Bottom area empty from ~660 down, but consistent. The subtitle under the gradient line: "新增芯片适配：2SFBL · SD · PMU/DVFS · LCDC/EPIC · GNSS · BLE | 板级改动：20 条抽换件 / 19 文件" — hmm "2SFBL" seems odd (maybe 2S Fall? whatever, content). Text small but legible at projection? It's small gray text ~ fine. Pass.

Wait — check the gradient short line on page 5: it appears above the subtitle at same position. Yes present.

Page 6: Three phone UI screenshots (P05, P03, P07) — third one (P07 菜单) appears cropped at bottom: the screenshot ends mid-"系统" section, cut off at bottom edge ("电量" partially visible cut). Compare first two screenshots: they end with rounded bottom bezel; third screenshot is cut off at the bottom — it shows the menu screen truncated, no bottom bezel, ending abruptly at same height as others. Look closely: P07 image bottom edge is cut mid-content — the "系统" section header and "电量" item are sliced. The other two screenshots show complete screens with bottom bezels. So P07 screenshot appears cropped/clipped — destructive cropping. Hmm, but is it a deliberate "bleed" crop? The caption "P07 菜单" is below. The first two show full phone screens with rounded corners at bottom; the third is cut flat at bottom edge with content sliced ("电量" text half visible). That looks like unintended destructive cropping or aspect mismatch: the third screenshot is same width but content taller, cut at container bottom. Actually looking at the render: P07 top aligns with others, bottom edge aligns with others, but the content within is cut — meaning the image is cropped, not scaled. The visible slice cuts through "电量" row. Is that a defect? The user explicitly asks: "截图/地图/GIF 首帧是否变形、被裁、比例正确" — cropped screenshots should be reported. The first two are complete screens; the third one is cut mid-content with no bottom bezel — inconsistent with the other two, reads as clipped.

Also the status bar strip below (19:40 ...) — wide strip, looks fine, caption below.

Hmm, let me reconsider: maybe P07 is intentionally showing a partial screen? The other two both have visible bottom bezel and rounded corners. P07 lacks bottom bezel and content is sliced mid-row — that's destructive cropping. I'll flag as Visual fail on page 6.

Also right column items (图形栈/信息架构/半透半反/图标) aligned, fine.

Let me zoom in to confirm P07 crop before flagging. I could crop the image region with Python? That's "analysis" — reading the image is allowed; using bash with Python PIL to crop is just for my inspection, not re-rendering the deliverable. That's fine — it doesn't modify anything. Let me crop the region of s-06 around the three screenshots' bottoms.

Actually I can be fairly confident from the rendered image: the third screenshot clearly ends with a horizontal cut through content ("系统" header and an item with icon, then "电量" text partially sliced at the very bottom edge). Meanwhile P05 and P03 both show complete rounded bezel bottoms. I'll verify with a zoom to be sure.

thinking:
Confirmed: P07 screenshot is cut mid-content — the "系统" section header and the "电量" row are sliced at the bottom edge, with no bottom bezel, while P05 and P03 show complete screens. This is destructive cropping of the third screenshot. Visual fail on page 6.

Continue with pages 7-8.

Page 7: Horizontal bar comparisons. Four rows: label left, bar middle, values "27.2 → 21.9", right big percentage. Bars: teal for row1 (filled ~72% of track, representing 21.9 vs 27.2? The "after" value relative to max?), blue row2 filled ~76%, teal row3 ~66%, purple row4 tiny ~8% (17 vs 195 — consistent). Bar fills appear to encode the reduced value relative to original (21.9/27.2≈0.80... bar ~72%? close-ish; 43.7/61.0≈0.72, bar ~76%... hmm approximate). Not going to nitpick bar length accuracy without measuring; the encoding reads plausibly as "after/original". Fine. Layout aligned, spacing even. Bottom footnotes row of three items aligned. There's a moderate empty band between bars section and footnotes, acceptable. Pass.

Wait — check bar proportions more carefully? Row 1: 27.2→21.9, filled fraction ~ (960-505)/(1070-505)? Let me estimate: track from x≈505 to 1070 (565 px), fill ends ≈960, so fill ≈ 455/565 ≈ 0.80 ≈ 21.9/27.2 = 0.805. Good. Row 2: track 505→1070, fill ends ≈908 → 403/565 ≈ 0.713 ≈ 43.7/61.0 = 0.716. Good. Row 3: fill ends ≈885 → 380/565 ≈ 0.67 ≈ 1.94/2.88 = 0.673. Good. Row 4: fill ends ≈553 → 48/565 ≈ 0.085 ≈ 17/195 = 0.087. Good — bars encode after/before accurately. Nice.

Page 8: Left column 4 numbered steps (01 切 / 02 找 / 03 画 / 04 补) with divider lines; right side: large map image + two smaller maps (day zoomed, night dark). The night map bottom-right — is it cut? It appears to end at same bottom edge as big map. Fine. Captions below maps. The bottom-right night map: right edge at 1533, big map right edge 1287... the small maps column extends to right margin ~1533, consistent with other pages' content width (1533). OK.

Map aspect: big map ~ (805→1287 wide = 482, 175→565 high = 390) → 482/390 ≈ 1.24. Tiles are square 256; showing a region — maps can be any crop, fine, not distorted (streets look natural, no stretching visible). Night map appears to be same region at night, dark. The top-right small map: (1298→1533 = 235 wide, 175→365 = 190 high). Fine.

One thing: step rows — the divider line above 01 starts at content left and extends to ~757 (half width). Rows are evenly spaced. The formula "x(y+1) = x(y) + dx/dy" at bottom left with note. Layout fine.

Empty space at bottom of page 8 (formula at ~710, footer at 845) — fine.

Pass for 8. Actually check: night map (dark) — is it squashed? Its region 1298→1533 wide (235), 375→565 high (190). Compare with the day small map above: 235×190. Both same size. Contents look natural. OK.

Continue 9-10.

Page 9: Five cards with top accent bars (teal/blue/purple/teal/blue), equal size, aligned. Bottom headline + sub. Cards mostly empty bottom half but uniform. Top accent bars: card tops have colored strip. Fine. Pass.

Page 10: Two phone screenshots left (设备 page and map playback), both look complete with bottom nav visible (first screenshot shows bottom nav partially? The first screenshot bottom shows nav icons "骑行/记录/设置" — visible but slightly cut? It shows icons row at bottom edge. It appears complete-ish; bottom row of icons visible with labels cut? Let me look: bottom of first screenshot shows icons with tiny labels partially visible at the very bottom edge — seems the phone screen itself includes the nav bar; the labels under icons appear slightly clipped by the image bottom edge? Hard to tell. The second screenshot ends with "00:04:17 · 3.14 公里" black bar — complete.

The map screenshot: any distortion? Map looks natural. Right column: rows 规划/通知/星历/升级/离线 with divider lines, aligned. Headline below. Pass.

Actually check first screenshot bottom edge: there's a nav bar with 3 icons, labels partially visible ("骑行"?). It reads as the app's own bottom nav, slightly tight to the edge — that's how the screenshot is. Fine.

Continue 11-12.

Page 11: Big teal "0" left, caption below; right side 4 stat rows with divider lines. Layout OK. Left column: "0" huge at top-left, then caption "次看门狗复位" at ~525, with two sub lines. The big 0 sits between y~185-350; left column otherwise empty below caption — fine. Right rows evenly spaced. Pass.

Page 12: Left rows 设备侧/取证/开发侧/审查 with dividers; right card "SKILL 速查" with 4 rows and note. Bottom headline + mono URL. Layout aligned. Right card: rows aligned, dividers between rows. The card bottom has note "4 份 references". Balanced enough. Pass.

Continue 13-15.

Page 13: Three columns (自研/基于/交付与复现), each with label + lines. Column 1 text wraps "板级 · 骑行应用 · Flutter App / 地图工具链 · AI Skill" — second line starts flush left, fine. Column 2: "openvela · NuttX · LVGL · / OpenStreetMap （ ODbL ）" — line break after "·" leaves trailing dot at line end; slightly awkward but acceptable? "（ ODbL ）" spacing with full-width parens plus spaces is a bit loose but not a defect per se. Middle band empty (large white gap between top columns ending ~300 and 板级约定 row at ~518). There's a large empty middle zone — page is sparse but not broken. Bottom rows fine. Hmm, is the emptiness a "visible imbalance"? The content occupies top 35% and bottom 40% with a gap; it's airy but symmetric. I'd pass, maybe note. Actually the gap between column text end (~300) and 板级约定 (~518) is ~200px of pure white across full width, plus below 固件 row (~635) to footer (~845) another ~200px empty. The page reads top-heavy then sparse. For a defense deck this is acceptable minimalism; not a defect that blocks presenting. Pass.

Page 14: Same three-column structure. Column 1 text: "公路 / 通勤 / 长途。成品码表贵、闭源、云锁定；手机支架耗电、分心。" wraps with "分心。" on second line — starts with two chars then period: "分心。" alone-ish? Actually second line is "分心。" — that's a two-character orphan line ending a sentence. Chinese line-breaking: a line starting with "分心。" — no punctuation at line start issue (。 is not at start; 分 starts). Orphan short line is common. Column 3 second line ends "复用到 / 别的运动设备。" — "别" split from "复制到别的" — "复用到别的运动设备" broke as "可复制到" end line then "别的运动设备。" — that's fine (别 is not punctuation). Column 2: "…没有账 / 号和骑行云" — "账号" split across lines ("账" end of line 1, "号" starts line 2). That's normal CJK wrapping; acceptable in Chinese typesetting (no rule against splitting words mid-way; Chinese wraps anywhere). OK.

Large empty middle again (~280 to ~520). Same airy style. Pass.

Page 15 next.

Page 15: THANKS black-background light-band slide. "THANKS" large white, gradient short line below (centered), subtitle "感谢各位评委老师聆听，欢迎提问与交流", then small "Helm One · 开源骑行码表 · Apache-2.0". Text sits over dark area above the ribbon — contrast fine. The small line "Helm One · 开源骑行码表 · Apache-2.0" sits over the dark ribbon area — slightly lower contrast but readable at gray-on-dark. Position stable, centered. MI logo top right present.

Check the subtitle contrast: white text over dark, ok. The small gray line over the purple/blue ribbon edge — "开源骑行码表" part sits over darker area; readable.

Now double-check page 2's empty card bottoms and whether any page has gradient line inconsistency. On content pages, the gradient short line under the title: page 2 at x≈85-140 under title. Page 11: the line under title appears at x≈85-148, same. Page 5's line appears slightly wider (85-148?) and the subtitle text sits right under it. Let me compare quickly across pages by cropping the title zone of a few pages to verify the gradient line and eyebrow positions are identical.

Also check footers: "2026 首届 openvela AI 硬件开发者大赛" bottom right with divider line above — present on all content pages (2-14). Present.

Let me verify gradient line consistency across pages 2-14 with a quick montage crop.

{"command": "cd /tmp && python3 -I -c "
from PIL import Image
import glob
files = sorted(glob.glob('/home/jinsc/SDK/vela/ppt/.build/render_tpl/s-*.png'))
ims=[]
for f in files[1:14]:
    im = Image.open(f).crop((60, 30, 700, 150))
    ims.append((f.split('/')[-1], im))
W = 640; H = 120
canvas = Image.new('RGB', (W, H*len(ims)), 'white')
for i,(name,im) in enumerate(ims):
    canvas.paste(im, (0, i*H))
canvas.save('/tmp/titles_stack.png')
print('ok', len(ims))

thinking:
The eyebrow, title and gradient line positions are consistent across pages 2–14. Page 5's gradient line is followed by the subtitle text immediately — consistent position.

One thing on page 5: the gradient line appears wider? In the stack, page 5's line at row 4 looks similar length. Fine.

Now confirm footer consistency across pages 2-14 — all showed the bottom-right text and divider. From the full-page reads, yes.

Now the only defect found: page 6 third screenshot (P07 菜单) cropped mid-content. Also check page 6: status bar strip (19:40) is a wide crop of a phone status bar — intentionally a strip, captioned "状态栏五态". Its corners are square, no bezel — intentional strip. OK.

Also double-check page 2 cards vs page 3: card heights equal within page. Yes.

Check page 2 more: cards have big empty lower halves (text ends ~430, card ends ~678) — uniform across all 3, consistent style; not flagging.

Page 9: same pattern; uniform.

Now, is P07 crop really "destructive"? Compare: P05 and P03 images are full phone screens with rounded bottom bezels visible; P07 lacks the bezel and cuts through the "电量" row mid-glyph. Yes, destructive crop. It also makes the three thumbnails inconsistent (two complete screens + one truncated). This is exactly the user's check item 3 (截图是否被裁). Fail page 6, Visual.

Everything else passes. Overall: 14/15 pass; one cropped screenshot on page 6.

Output format requested by dispatch: {"page":N,"verdict":"pass|fail","issues":["具体到元素与位置"],"fix":"一句可执行修法"} — one line per page, then a final overall sentence. The dispatch overrides the default schema slightly (issues as string array + fix). I'll follow the dispatch format. For passing pages, include no issues/fix or empty? The example in my system prompt shows pass with just verdict. The dispatch format shows issues/fix fields; I'll include them only on fail pages to keep lines clean — actually the dispatch example implies fields exist; safest: pass lines just {"page":N,"verdict":"pass"} plus fix omitted... The dispatch says 每页一行 JSON with that shape. I'll include "issues":[] and "fix":"" for pass? That's noisy. I'll include issues/fix only when fail, which still matches the shape per line reasonably. Hmm — to be safe and literal, include the keys with empty values on pass pages. I'll do: pass lines as {"page":N,"verdict":"pass"} — the dispatcher likely parses issues only on fail. But the requested shape explicitly includes issues and fix keys. I'll include them for fails and keep pass minimal — this matches my base protocol example too. Actually the base protocol example shows pass without issues. The dispatch format adds fix. I'll output fails with issues+fix, passes plain. Final sentence overall judgment at the end.
